title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
abstract: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

bite.hook: Scrambled noisy quantum states settle into universal patterns dictated purely by their error channels.
tldr: Investigated whether mixed quantum states undergoing noisy scrambling reach universal projected distributions.
Derived analytical solutions across dual-unitary circuits and Haar-random models, verified by numerical simulations.
Demonstrated the late-time ensemble is universally determined by the normalized Choi state of the noise channel.
bite.whyItMatters: Real quantum systems always suffer from noise; understanding universal late-time states helps predict how scrambled information degrades in quantum hardware.
bite.eli5: If you mix a hot drink, it loses all memory of how you stirred it. Similarly, noisy quantum systems eventually forget their initial state, settling into a pattern set purely by the noise itself.

glossary.shortDef: The convergence of measurement-projected quantum ensembles toward universal random distributions.
glossary.eli5Def: When a scrambled quantum system looks completely random, even across delicate sub-measurements.

glossary.shortDef: A statistical ensemble of different quantum states, typical of noisy or open systems.
glossary.eli5Def: A quantum state that is messy and partially random, usually because of environmental noise.

glossary.shortDef: A bipartite quantum state isomorphic to a quantum channel via the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism.
glossary.eli5Def: A clever mathematical representation of a quantum process as if it were a physical state.

glossary.shortDef: Quantum circuits that remain unitary under space-time exchange, enabling exact solvable models.
glossary.eli5Def: Toy quantum circuits that allow information to flow smoothly along both space and time directions.
